(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA)
1.
The accident is not in dispute and the liability of the insurer to pay the compensation is also not in dispute.

2. The Tribunal has awarded the following sums:
1. Pain and sufferings Rs.25,000/-
2. Loss of amenities & Rs.20,000/-

sentences.text:
Medical Expenses Rs.1,86,000/-
Total Rs.5,72,000/-
NC: 2024:KHC-K:6845 3.
The claimant being dissatisfied, is an appeal.

It is contended that the income of Rs.7,500/-
applied by the Tribunal is incorrect and consequently the sums awarded towards loss of income would be inadequate.
It is also argued that the sums awarded under the other heads are also on the lower side.
4. The Tribunal has assessed the disability at 20% to the whole body taking into consideration the evidence of PW.2.
In my view, this assessment cannot be found fault with.
However the application of Rs.7,500/- as the notional income would be contrary to the sum of Rs.8000/- fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for accidents of the year 2015 .
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.3,26,400/- (Rs.8,000/- x 12 x 17 x 20%) towards loss of future income.
5. The Tribunal has awarded a sum Rs.25,000/- towards pain and suffering Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.

In my view, this would have to be enhanced to Rs.50,000/- and Rs.40,000/-
respectively.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards medical attendant charges, food and nutrition and transportation charges.
In my view, since the claimant was hospitalized for 21 days, it would be appropriate to enhance it to Rs.30,000/-.
7. Since the claimant was hospitalized for 21 days, it would be appropriate to take the laid up period as three months and award a sum of Rs.24,000/- in this regard.
8. The sum of Rs.1,86,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards medical expenses is affirmed.

9. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled for the following sums:
1. Pain and sufferings Rs.50,000/-
2. Loss of amenities & Rs.40,000/-
pleasure 3.

6. Medical Expenses Rs.1,86,000/-
Total Rs.6,56,400/-
NC: 2024:KHC-K:6845 10.

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.6,56,400/- as against Rs.5,72,000/-, along with interest at the rate of six per cent per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
11. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
12. The deposit and release of the enhanced compensation amount shall be made as per the ratio adopted by the Tribunal.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
